source_boundary.preserved_question_intent: Compare java.util.HashMap and java.util.Hashtable, especially synchronization, null handling, API history and modern selection.

claims.text: HashMap is unsynchronized and requires external synchronization for concurrent structural modification, whereas Hashtable is documented as synchronized; Java SE 21 recommends ConcurrentHashMap for a thread-safe highly-concurrent map.
HashMap permits null values and the null key, while Hashtable requires non-null keys and values and throws NullPointerException for null key/value operations such as put.
Hashtable predates the Collections Framework, extends Dictionary and was retrofitted to implement Map, while HashMap is an AbstractMap-based Collections Framework implementation.
HashMap's fail-fast iterator behavior is best-effort and must not be used as a correctness or synchronization mechanism.

JDK 21 GA implementation details such as HashMap tree bins and Hashtable's internal synchronized/rehash structure are version-bound implementation details, not the primary cross-version semantic comparison.

writer_constraints: Use the Java class name Hashtable, while acknowledging source wording may say HashTable.
Do not reduce the answer to speed claims; performance depends on synchronization needs and workload.
Do not claim Hashtable makes arbitrary multi-call business invariants atomic.
Do not treat HashMap fail-fast behavior as thread safety.
Recommend ConcurrentHashMap as the official modern highly-concurrent alternative when thread-safe high concurrency is required.
Keep JDK 21 implementation internals explicitly version-bound.
